data.bug_class: use-of-uninitialized-value (MSan) / possible heap-buffer-overflow in output sample conversion paths
data.rationale: The fuzz target (oss-fuzz/tool_flac.c) wraps src/flac/main.c, so all flac CLI paths are reachable; decoding is the dominant path exercised by the seed corpus (-d with --cue/--skip/replaygain variants). write_callback converts decoded samples through the stack union 'ubuf' and through FLAC__replaygain_synthesis__apply_gain. Several branches here write only part of ubuf while later code reads more (e.g. the 16-bit fast-path memcpy of sizeof(int32)*wide_samples-2 bytes followed by interleaving loops), and the replaygain path passes bps+shift as target_bps with a dither context whose validity depends on state set in the metadata callback (line 1599). The build configures SANITIZER=memory, so the target bug class is use-of-uninitialized-value, most plausibly triggered in these conversion/replaygain branches. Confidence is LOW: ~9 minutes of libFuzzer runs on the seed corpus and hand-crafted option combinations (decode/encode, --keep-foreign-metadata, --apply-replaygain, --cue, -a) did not reproduce a sanitizer report, so this is static-analysis-based reasoning rather than an empirically confirmed stack trace. A deeper targeted fuzz (larger inputs, full option dictionary, replaygain+bps-shift combinations) should be run next to confirm the exact line.
